name: Granular Corneal Dystrophy Type II

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Granular Corneal Dystrophy Type II

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic granular and lattice-like stromal opacities on slit-lamp examination
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the TGFBI gene, commonly R124H mutation
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic corneal opacities plus identification of pathogenic TGFBI mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by genetic confirmation; family history aids but is not mandatory.

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing TGFBI gene mutation (commonly R124H)
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing granular and lattice stromal deposits
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) demonstrating stromal opacities and thickening
genetic: Autosomal dominant mutations in TGFBI gene
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Only granular stromal deposits without lattice lines
Predominantly lattice stromal deposits without granular opacities

redFlags: Recurrent painful corneal erosions unresponsive to treatment
Signs of secondary infection or corneal ulceration
references: Weiss JS, Møller HU, Lisch W, et al. IC3D classification of corneal dystrophies—edition 2. Cornea. 2015;34(2):117-159.
Munier FL, Korvatska E, Djemaï A, et al. Kerato-epithelin mutations in four 5q31-linked corneal dystrophies. Nat Genet. 1997;15(3):247-251.
